commands.desc: Lists container images referenced by active pods (status.phase Running or Pending; Succeeded and Failed pods are excluded, terminating pods remain until removed), reading spec.containers, spec.initContainers, and spec.ephemeralContainers. --match filters by case-sensitive substring over the image reference exactly as written in the pod spec: repeatable, values OR, no OCI normalization (a bare nginx:1.25 does not match docker.io); anchor with delimiters, e.g. --match registry.old.corp/ for a registry. --match never inspects image contents. --by workload resolves each pod's controller owner chain and reports one row per image and owning workload object (apiVersion, kind, name, uid) with the count of pods controlled by exactly that object; owner-resolution failures degrade to the first-level reference plus a warning. Partial access degrades rather than fails: a collector this caller cannot read is named in data.degraded ({section, state, code, target}) with one paired warning each, and the command still exits 0. Cluster resolution and the pod list are required and hard-error; with --all-clusters the management cluster list is required, zero listed clusters is a verified-empty success, and every listed cluster failing its scan is an error. Degradable sections: ownerResolution (partial, target = the canonical owner identity apiVersion|kind|namespace|name|uid, cluster-id prefixed under --all-clusters), clusters (partial, target = cluster id, --all-clusters only).

commands.desc: One document answering what state a cluster is in, what it is made of, and how nodes join it: the management cluster identity (id, name, state, kubernetesVersion — observed version first, the provisioning spec's desired version for pending clusters, empty when neither exists), its agent connectivity (agent.connected and agent.ready from the management Cluster's Connected and Ready conditions with the failing condition's message, preferring Connected's; the section is present only when those conditions report an explicit True or False (Unknown is not a verdict and never reads as disconnected) and each field only when its own condition does; a disconnected agent or a False Ready condition adds a warning — the provisioning-derived status cannot see an agent outage), the provisioning.cattle.io Cluster's ready flag (derived from the Ready condition when present; falls back to status.ready) and conditions, its machine pools (name, machineConfigRef, quantity, roles), its members (ClusterRoleTemplateBindings with display names resolved from Users and UserAttributes, each row reporting principal, displayName, role, binding (the CRD object name), and system; a failed binding read omits the members field from JSON while the text card renders a members-unavailable marker, with a warning naming the cause; enrichment failure only drops display names, never rows; entries whose principal id is system-prefixed (Rancher's system principals, e.g. system://provisioning/...) carry system: true (Rancher-internal accounts, not operator grants)), its machines (CAPI Machine objects in fleet-default filtered by the cluster.x-k8s.io/cluster-name label; each entry reports name, phase, and the first failing condition message — preferring conditions whose reason contains "Error"; a failed LIST omits the machines field from JSON while the text card renders a machines-unavailable marker, with a warning naming the cause; absent when the provisioning cluster was not found), and the default registration token's node-join pair (nodeCommand/insecureNodeCommand), import pair (command/insecureCommand), and manifestUrl (on an imported cluster — provisioning spec.rkeConfig absent — notApplicable lists the node-join fields that are present but do not apply; fields are annotated, never dropped). The registration section is withheld by default because it embeds a live cluster join token (a credential that lets anyone add nodes to the cluster); pass --registration to fetch and show it. Sections degrade independently: provisioningNote marks a confirmed missing provisioning Cluster; an unavailable or ambiguous lookup and a failed registration read omit their sections with a warning naming the cause. Partial access degrades rather than fails: a collector this caller cannot read is named in data.degraded ({section, state, code, target}) with one paired warning each, and the command still exits 0. Cluster resolution and the management Cluster GET are required and hard-error. Degradable sections: provisioning (unavailable — the correlation, one entry covering the status, machinePools, and machines it leaves absent), machines (unavailable — a machine list that failed after a successful correlation), members (unavailable — the binding list; display-name enrichment failures stay advisory warnings), registration (unavailable — the token read).

commands.desc: Compatibility adapter for kubeconfigs generated by Rancher with kubeconfig-generate-token disabled, which invoke the legacy CLI's `rancher token`. New integrations and agents use `auth get-token`; this command exists so existing kubeconfigs keep working after swapping the binary. --user is the cache-slot key and basic-auth username default; stored-login selection follows server-ranking, not --user.

commands.desc: Groups results by --by (namespace|project|node|pod). --namespace, --project, and --node are filters that narrow every grouping: --node keeps only pods scheduled on that node; --namespace with --project requires a member namespace. --by node accepts only --node; combining --by node with --namespace or --project is a validation error. --project without --by returns member-namespace rows (namespace grouping filtered to the project). --by project --project X returns a single project bucket. Partial access degrades rather than fails: a collector this caller cannot read is named in data.degraded ({section, state, code, target}) with one paired warning each, and the command still exits 0. Required collectors hard-error: cluster resolution and the pod list always; project resolution and the membership list with --project; the project and namespace maps with --by project; the node list with --by node, or the named node GET with --by node --node N. Degradable section: metrics (unavailable — requests and limits stay). A scope that resolves to zero namespaces is verified empty: no pod or metrics read is issued.
